title: Independent verification of the #543 bit moment using binomial enclosures
head: bdc9317efd6d928a0f050159670d1316ba5f4c5b
body:
This independently confirms the strict bit-moment bracket from #543 consumed by #626 at adjacent `10^-24` endpoints, including the exceptional-set fallback charge. Omitting that charge changes the upper endpoint from rejection to acceptance.

`research/pr543-binomial-audit/verify.py` uses outward-rounded rational generalized-binomial terms and a geometric tail bound, without importing the existing logarithm/exponential pricing engines. The package includes an exact certificate and source pins. The audit takes the paid profile and fallback formula as inputs and checks their numerical consequence; their construction-level justification remains inherited. It does not change the selected bound or formally verify the multiplication theorem.

## Reproduce

From the repository root, using Python’s standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/pr543-binomial-audit/verify.py
```

Expected output:

```text
PASS_PR543_BINOMIAL_MOMENT
Strict adjacent 10^-24 endpoints; 71 algebraic controls; 3 mathematical controls; 8 rejected inputs.
```

The controls check rational-power enclosures by exact integer-power comparisons and demonstrate that equal call count and rank mass do not determine the moment. Disposable-copy mutation tests rejected missing tails, downward-rounded upper terms, an omitted fallback coefficient, and altered source or certificate bytes.

The checker passed on Python 3.12.3, including with `-O`; `make selected-record-check` also passed. The full `make verify` and `make frontier626-verify` suites were not run.
